open_points.subject: A20 rule 6 Linux execution contract
open_points.text: A release runs on Linux and on no other host, no version named, and its Python is CPython 3.12 (owner, 2026-11-25). Another system, or a Linux or file system on which a call Registry's rules rely on — opening a file without following a link, binding a listening socket, renaming, flushing — does not act as Linux documents it, is unsupported: Registry neither tests for it nor defines what it does there.
open_points.question: Which Linux and file-system semantics are required—particularly the exact no-link, exclusive-bind, rename atomicity, and flush/durability guarantees—and which document or version defines them?
options: Require the stated operations to have explicitly enumerated Linux semantics on every supported Linux and file system.
Name a minimum kernel, libc and supported file-system baseline whose documented semantics are authoritative.
Leave each generated module to select the Linux calls and semantics on which its own rules rely.
open_points.default_guess: Define the required observable semantics explicitly and treat any Linux or file system lacking them as unsupported.

witness.initial: A release is installed on Linux using a file system whose rename or flush behavior differs among plausible readings of the unnamed Linux documentation.
events: Registry replaces or flushes a file while preserving a rule that depends on atomic replacement or durability.
One implementer relies on rename completion alone; another also flushes the containing directory because that is required by the Linux/file-system semantics they selected.
outcomes: After a reported successful operation, a crash may lose the replacement.
After a reported successful operation, the replacement survives the same crash.
witness.observer: The owner after recovery from the crash.

open_points.subject: A20 rule 6 host-capability probes
open_points.text: it uses the host's facilities as Linux documents them and tests for the presence of none
open_points.question: What exactly counts as testing for the presence of a host facility: platform or version checks, feature probes such as hasattr, attempting a required call and handling its unsupported error, or any inspection of an attribute?
options: Forbid only proactive platform, version and feature-detection branches; required calls may still report their ordinary failures.
Forbid every availability check and every unsupported-feature fallback, including handling an unsupported error specially.
Forbid any attribute inspection, as the Formal invariants passage can literally be read.
open_points.default_guess: Forbid proactive platform and feature probes and fallbacks, while allowing required calls to fail through their specified failure path.

witness.initial: A generated module needs a Linux-only facility exposed as an optional runtime attribute.
events: One implementer calls hasattr before using the facility.
Another invokes the facility directly and handles the runtime error if it is unavailable.
outcomes: The first implementation is rejected as a prohibited presence test and the second is accepted.
Both implementations are rejected because either behavior tests or reacts to the facility's presence.
witness.observer: The Factory gate and the developer whose generated module it admits or rejects.

open_points.subject: A20 Formal invariants and Required tests
open_points.text:
None: kept outside Registry's checks — rules 1–4 and rule 6's host and
Python by the release process and its installation (rule 5), and rule 6's
"tests for the presence of none" by the Factory's static gate on every
generated module, which rejects any probe of an attribute — so the running
dependencies are the release's (name, version, digest) and the host is
Linux, which no note or check of Registry's code can show.
open_points.question: Is the absence of host-capability probes a formal invariant of generated Registry code, and, if so, what must its Required tests item show? If it is not an invariant, what status gives the Factory gate its required rejection behavior?
options: Declare a formal invariant that generated Registry code contains none of the defined prohibited probes, and add a Required tests item stating the positive and negative cases the Factory check must show.
Remove the Factory-gate guarantee and retain no Registry-code invariant.
Classify the rule as an external release-process constraint and state how that process demonstrates it without claiming a static code gate.
open_points.default_guess: Declare the no-probe property as a formal invariant and add a Required tests item that shows prohibited probes are rejected and permitted ordinary attribute use is accepted.

witness.initial: All four listed A20 Required tests pass for a release, but a generated Registry module contains a host-capability probe.
events: The release process runs Required tests 1–4.
One Factory implementation has the claimed static gate; another treats A20's declaration of no formal invariant literally and has no such check.
outcomes: The module is rejected before release.
The same module is admitted because every stated Required test passes.
witness.observer: The release author and the user receiving or not receiving the release.

open_points.subject: A20 exact CPython version selection
open_points.text: A release runs on Linux and on no other host, no version named, and its Python is CPython 3.12 (owner, 2026-11-25).
open_points.question: Which exact CPython 3.12 patch release is fixed for a particular release?
options: Pin the current selected CPython 3.12.x patch version in each release.
Keep one exact CPython 3.12.x patch version fixed across several releases until a dependency update release changes it.
open_points.default_guess: Pin one exact CPython 3.12.x patch version in the release manifest.
consequences: Selecting a newer patch changes the runtime dependency and requires a new verified release under A20 rule 3.
Retaining an older patch preserves reproducibility but may defer runtime fixes.
open_points.requirement: A release names every dependency it runs with, at an exact version, with its digest: every Python package, direct or transitive, by the digest of its distribution file; the Python version; and the base image of VM Platform's Registry environment by its digest, which fixes the system libraries and the store's engine.

open_points.subject: A21 security review after the A20 change
open_points.text: A change to a decision a category names reopens this review.
open_points.question: What is the recorded result of reopening the dependencies category after the 2026-11-25 change to A20 added the Linux-only, CPython 3.12 and no-capability-probe obligations?
options: Record a new review of the dependencies category, expand its affected subjects to the host/runtime assumptions, and state whether its outcome changes.
Decide that the added obligations are outside the dependencies category, while still recording the reopening and the basis for that conclusion.
Change A21 rule 2 so that only specified kinds of changes reopen a category.
open_points.default_guess: Reopen dependencies, include the Linux host, CPython runtime and no-probe constraint in the affected scope, and record the resulting APPLICABLE outcome.

witness.initial: A21 names A20 as the sole reference of the dependencies category, and A20 is changed on 2026-11-25.
events: The change adds Linux-only execution and a generated-code constraint.
One continuation applies A21 rule 2 and reruns the category review; another treats the earlier 2026-11-24 A20 review as still sufficient.
outcomes: The security review records whether the new host/runtime assumptions preserve its outcome.
The review remains marked complete without evaluating the newly added obligations.
witness.observer: The owner and the later agent relying on A21's claim of a complete review.

open_points.subject: A20 Factory static-gate claim
open_points.text:
rule 6's
"tests for the presence of none" by the Factory's static gate on every
generated module, which rejects any probe of an attribute
open_points.rule:
Доказательство —
декларация, а не проза: фраза «её читает гейт» читателя не доказывает.
open_points.question: Replace the prose-only Factory-gate claim with a declared gate-readable policy whose kind, reader, fields and applicable modules are present in tools/gate_rules_reads.py, or remove the claim that the Factory gate enforces it.
